utterances.text: Well, I don't see any contradictory either in my statement or in my later evidence in the Krnojelac case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So, according to you, there is no conflict whatsoever here.

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Well, the truth is that at that time my memory was far better than it has been over the past couple of years, because at that time I did not use as many psychiatric medicines as I am using today.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now I will briefly take you back to Montenegro again because there was one thing that I wanted to clarify. Of the 25 people of Muslim ethnicity that were taken to the police station, why is it that only five of you were detained?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Well, I'm not clear on that myself. I don't understand it. Because the policemen who was sent by Mr. Stevanovic and Mr. Zdravko Matovic who were on the ground floor, those policemen brought a list with them with the five names, the names of the five men who were supposed to be detained, whereas the rest were let go.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the same transcript, on page 12, that's page 2944 of the transcript, beginning with line 1, you say the following. I will read this out in English: [In English] "A. Well, my assumption was - and I believe I spoke about it - was that those who were in that group of 25, that Mr. Stefanovic did not know them sufficiently well, and that he picked out precisely those amongst us whom he knew." Question by my colleague Bakrac: "And did you mention this reason to the OTP? "A. I think I did. "Q. You told the OTP that you thought you had been picked out as prominent men whom they believed participating in the SDA activities in Foca. That is at variance with what you told us today. "A. Yes. That fact is true." [Interpretation] My question is this: Do you know why, out of the 25 men, the five of you were picked out? Was what you said at the Krnojelac trial or what you said in your statement or what you've actually said here today? Which is correct or don't you see any difference?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Well, in my statement, you will find the same thing that I said during my evidence in Krnojelac. I said that I could only assume why I was one of the men on the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, in the Krnojelac testimony, reference is made to the statement. Which statement was that? I do not know exactly. And I take it that you have compared it. And where do we find it in the statement, if it's our statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is one of these two statements. I did compare but I didn't jot it down. Can I use the break it check -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I think we have found it meanwhile. That's the 1995 statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In Krnojelac it is an assumption and here it is a presumption. Let's stick to the facts and what the witness knows. Because I was a bit -- and if it was then put by your colleague Mr. Bakrac that it is contradictory, it should be clear that it was only a presumption which he expressed in his statement just as it was an assumption as he expressed in Krnojelac. And let's try not to conduct this case on the basis of assumptions or presumptions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. RM013, can we then agree that you don't actually know the reason why you were singled out of that group of 25 men. You and four other men?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Well, from -- as I sit here, if I were to justify or say why it was that -- well, I think that's not necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, if you know, if they told you, or if you know by any other reason, tell us. If you are just guessing, then refrain from doing that. And then you apparently do not know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. [Interpretation] Well, I think it suffices what I've already said in my assumption. I can't see any other reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I know that you were already informed by Judge Fluegge, I found the -- where I found in his statement. It's in Serbian version, page 4, paragraph 4, and also in English version, page 4, paragraph 4. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Without my colleagues, I would be lost, Mr. Lukic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like us to briefly discuss the arrangements of the KP Dom where you were detained. Let's start from lorries. You spoke of lorries at page 2947 of the 13th of February, 2001, in the Krnojelac case. That's page 15 in e-court. The same transcript that we already have on our screens. You speak of lorries bringing food supplies. You mentioned a lorry coming from Uzice. It was a civilian lorry, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The licence plates it had were those of Titova Uzice. So that said it all.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In line 11 on that same page, you said that the driver was in civilian clothes; right?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then, at page 2947 - we need lines 22 to 25 - you say that when Krnojelac left - that's to say, after he was relieved of his duties - the conditions in the KP Dom changed. You said: "... yes, definitely." You went on to explain this. But let me ask you this: The conditions in the KP Dom improved. They changed for the better; right?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer, Witness, whether the circumstances changes for the better. Did they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then, at page 2949, page 17 in e-court of the same transcript, you say that you insisted with Dr. Dobrilovic -- [In English] Sorry, line 20 to 23? [Interpretation] And you asked him what you should do with your pneumonia and you said that you were only given two injections. The question was then: Which injections, antibiotics? And your answer was: Yes. Do you recall this part of your testimony; and do you confirm it?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was Gojko Jankovic's role in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Gojko Jankovic did not work for the KP Dom. That must be an error in the family name. Jokanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Gojko Jokanovic. You are right. Did he work at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was his profession?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: He worked in the health service, a medic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you receive your medication from him as well during your time in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Once, if I recall. I think it was painkillers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. MacGregor.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm looking at the transcript, and at least from the way I read it, it appears that the line of questioning is still referring to "he" and the witness clarified that "he, Jankovic, did not work there." The next question from counsel was repeating the name and the question is did he work at KP Dom. I'm not clear who is being spoken about. If you look above that, there's a doctor with a different last name being referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I can clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether it is it Jankovic or Jokanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Jokanovic. Yes, I think the witness was speaking of Jokanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you said that the person who worked in the health service, a medic, was Mr. Jokanovic, and he worked for the KP Dom is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: To make it more complicated in the transcript, line 24, which is on the screen now, the name is Gojko Jovanovic. That should be clarified too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But it -- well, there is a theatre piece comedy of errors. That is not what we're working in at this moment. But it's clear Gojko Jankovic is the person who did not work for the KP Dom. And the doctor, Jokanovic, did work for the KP Dom. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During your time in the KP Dom, did you move about the KP Dom freely at all times?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: No. I was not able to move freely. I was constantly under lock and key.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was there a period of time during your stay in the KP Dom that you were able to move freely?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Yes. That was the period when I was assigned to chop wood within the KP Dom compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it true that during this period of time you were able to freely interact with the inmates who within the KP Dom compound, you could be in contact with them?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Yes, I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's now discuss the four groups of persons you mentioned as having been taken out of the KP Dom and killed. Can you now tell us the names of the people who were in the first group?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: That would be very difficult without consulting my notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In other words, without consulting your notes, you would not be able to --

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: I can recall their names, but I sincerely doubt that I would be able to recall which particular group they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would it be helpful if you were to have your statement before you?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that how you want to proceed, then perhaps a hard copy could be given to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection, Ms. MacGregor, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: I have no objection. I have hard copies. Actually, the witness does have hard copies with him, in front of him now, if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh. The Chamber wasn't aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: If you could direct him which -- which statement we're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 1995, please. [Interpretation] Paragraph 39 on page 8. My apologies. We need page 7 and paragraph 36.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That should be P982.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We need the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I -- I went back to paragraph 36, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So page -- page 7 is the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you have paragraph 36 from your 1995 statement?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bear with me for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The first group, as indicated in this written statement, there are eight names.

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Nine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Were these people taken out, all of them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. MacGregor.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Your Honours, earlier today when we were proceeding through testimony about the 92 ter statements, an amendment was made to this paragraph to add a name. So I just wanted to bring that to the attention of counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That was the next list -- the next group, not this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The one with eight names. This one is with nine name.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Sorry. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's avoid confusion. My learned friend was referring to paragraph 40 and now we are with paragraph 36.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your view, are these the nine persons who were taken out on that first occasion and beaten up? You said that you observed these beatings.

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And there was the total of nine people; right?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I forgot to turn it off and then I forgot to turn it on. [Interpretation] We need page -- first, we need 1D792, page 24 in e-court, which is transcript page 2956 from the Krnojelac case of the 13th of February 2001. From line 14 to line 24. There, my learned friend Mr. Bakrac is listing these persons for you and says that -- or it is stated here that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the counsel please repeat his question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that Munib Veiz was also taken out with this group but that you forgot his name. So was Munib Veiz really taken out with this group?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: No, he was with the second group.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Also, on the same occasion, in line 21, my learned friend, Mr. Bakrac told you that you said on that day in that trial that Husein Rikalo was taken out in the second group, whereas here we see him listed as the fourth person in that first group. So was he taken out with the first or with the second group?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: I can't be sure that I could have stated something like this. Husein Rikalo was taken out with the first group.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Also in line 22, colleague Bakrac said to you that you stated on that day in this trial that Krunoslav Marinovic was also taken out in the first group. Was Krunoslav Marinovic taken out in the first group?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Krunoslav Marinovic was taken out in the third group.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Therefore, what you stated in respect of Munib Veiz, Husein Rikalo, and Krunoslav Marinovic in the trial against Krnojelac was not correct. Rather, what your statement says is correct?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Yes, the statement is correct. At the time I was giving this evidence, I must have mixed up the groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who was taken out of the inmates from your room?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Nail Hodzic, Seval Soro, Esad Kiselica, Kruno Marinovic, and I believe ... I don't recall anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now we need page 25 of this same transcript. That's page 2957 in the Krnojelac transcript, lines 23 through 25. And then it goes on to the next page. But here we see that my colleague Bakrac actually puts it to you that you had seen these three, that you had mentioned these three in your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now could we see the next page, 2958. We need it from the top of the page, 1 through 8. Lines 1 through 8. My colleague Bakrac puts it to you here that in the examination-in-chief in the Krnojelac case, you said that Esad Kiselica was not in your room. And then in line 3 you say: "Esad Kiselica was not in my room. I think I made a mistake." Which is correct? What you've said today, what you said in your statement, or your evidence in Krnojelac?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Only what I said in my statement is correct. There must have been some kind of confusion because it's impossible for me to remember all the men who have been and gone through my room, as it were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the Chamber is not assisted by the way in which you apparently are seeking to detect certain mistakes made by the witness. What the Chamber is interested in is to hear from this witness whether people detained with him in groups were taken away and what was their fate and not on whether the witness, after 20 years, remembers exactly who was in the first group or the second group. To the extent you wanted to establish that there may be minor inconsistencies, you have done so. The Chamber is not further assisted by continuing this exercise. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We just want to make submission that this goes for all four groups, that we could show the differences, but I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But is it your case that not groups of approximately the number of people having been detained there, is it your -- that -- is it your position that it was all invented by the witness, that these people did not die? Is that -- or are you establishing that some mistakes were made in the groups? We'd like to know that, what your position is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First we are testing the knowledge of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but that wasn't my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I cannot --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have told us that you want to further explore possible errors. Our -- my clear question, is it the position of the Defence that people did not disappear, were not detained, at least not these people, were not killed? Or is it that you want to establish that the witness not in every respect has been consistent in giving the names, putting them in groups, et cetera? Which of the two is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't think that the -- that Defence has to have any position to cross-examine this witness on these issues because he was -- he is testifying about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You can't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you are --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can tell you, we object in totality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. You object in totality what?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you ask me -- that those people are killed and that this gentleman knows about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So the position is that these people were not killed. That's your position.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What other position can I have?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, other positions are -- you could think of. But it's clear. If that's your position, then please proceed. Then minor mistakes in the grouping is for, as far as I understand, is for you an indication that the witness is reporting persons to have been killed which were not killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have to tell you, five -- five and six names, five names out of nine are wrong. And we have the testimony where he claims that he knows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We will then hear that. At least you've clarified your position. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your 1995 statement, we see these names quoted in the second group. That's paragraph 40. There's an additional name that was added to this because there were eight names in that group and now we have nine. Is it the case, for instance, that Seval Soro was in this group?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: No, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This morning in his evidence in-chief he told us who was the ninth person. Why do you mention another name that's not on that list, in this group?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Because, in Krnojelac, that name was in that group. And I will now read the Krnojelac transcript. I asked, again, 1D792, page 26. And we need line 9 up -- up to 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague Bakrac here cites the names of the men taken from your statement, your 1995 statement. Apparently you mentioned these eight names that appear in paragraph 40 as those, whereas in line 12 he asks you the following, and I will read in English: [In English] "That is what you listed in your first statement in 1995. Today you said to us that the following persons were taken out in the second group: Seval Soro, Mate Ivancic, Zulfo Veiz, Ekrem Tulek, Refik Cankusic. With the exception of Zulfo Veiz, the other persons do not correspond at all to those mentioned in your statement in 1995. How do you explain that?"

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: I don't know how relevant this question is, who was in what group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, relevant or not, would you please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I take it that you were still quoting from the transcript of the other case including the last question, "... how do you explain that?"

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That was in my --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- my question would be the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But before you put this question to the witness, I would like to know what he said earlier in his testimony. You are only quoting from the question of counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I -- I can read the rest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No. Counsel in that case was referring to his testimony that day earlier. So I don't know what the witness said in that case. This is only a quotation in a question put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can quote the answer. The answer, I quote: "I explained that by the following" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not what Judge Fluegge -- Judge Fluegge is seeking the source of where the witness said that Seval Soro, Mate Ivancic, Zulfo Veiz, Ekrem Tulek, and Refik Cankusic were taken out in the second group. Where is that to be found in this transcript? That's the question by Judge Fluegge.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can use the break to give you the exact reference for that. But I'm -- that -- it is in that transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But to put it that way to this witness is really confusing, and therefore it would be much more appropriate if you put his own evidence given in that case to the witness and then he can confirm or disagree.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will do that, Your Honour, after the break. May I continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, let us try and make this simple and short. Did you see or did you hear the people from the other group when they were taken out, or did you cover your head and your ears so you couldn't hear or see the people from the second group who were taken out?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: I -- I did see the men who were taken away, but there were occasions where, as you described it, I was forced to close my ears and eyes because I could not bear to hear the cries coming from the solitary cells, but that did not last long.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. But I'm asking you about this specific situation where the second group was being taken out.

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Well, that's what my answer referred to.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What did you see? What was it that you saw? Did you see when they were being taken out? Did you see how far they took them away? What is it that you could see or hear?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Well, of course I saw everything. They took them out and lined them up outside the admin -- the administrative building, but when the cries, when it was possible to hear the cries of the beatings because they beat them there, I could not bear to listen to that, so I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see when that group was taken out of KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: No, nor could I see that. But they were never returned to KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As you sit here today, do you remember that my colleague Bakrac told you that you had added some names? And how did that come about? Did you try and refresh your memory by talking to other detainees? Or is it just your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Well, of course, this is not all based on my knowledge alone. Because there was an organisation of detainees that was active --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. MacGregor.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's quite a compound question that it's not clear what's actually being asked of the witness. He first asked if he remembered something Mr. Bakrac said. Then he says how did that come about? Did you try to refresh your memory? Is that your knowledge? It's not clear what question is being asked of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The answer is only about the knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether he knows about all of what you did put to him. Is that ... Let's ... yes, it is a rather compound question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will -- I will cut it short.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it correct that you talked with other detainees about matters. You discussed them and that the knowledge that you are telling us about here is not yours alone?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Well, this is based on my knowledge, 99 per cent. About 1 per cent of the knowledge, I derived from other people, and that had to do with the arrangements of these groups and the names of the people who were being taken out in groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On page 27 of the transcript - and that's page 2959 of the transcript itself - we need to look at lines 20 and 21. Here, you talk about the third group. And, in line 20, you were asked by my colleague Bakrac whether other detainees had helped you to refresh your memory and you say, in line 21: "No. No. Absolutely no one held me." So what you've just told us is not correct.

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Well, this was a generalised answer. I wasn't helped by anyone. No one -- in the sense that no one dictated the list of the people who were killed in KP Dom. They only helped me with the order of the groups as they were taken out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it would be fair to read the next question and answer to the witness too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Trust me, I have only up to line 21. But maybe we can see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Line 22 reads can: "Q. You said that you made type written notes on the basis of other detainees' memories as well. "A. I made these notes in writing together with the other detainees. As concerns dates, the dates of exchanges and other events, I was not sure ..." So we should see another page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "... I was not sure of; I wasn't sure of their dates."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm looking at the clock. At the same time, before we take a break, Ms. MacGregor, as matters stand now, how much time would you need for re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I anticipate 15 to 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 15 to 20 minutes. Mr. Lukic, how much time would you still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I probably need one hour. And we have one day available this week. Friday is free.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you one question, Mr. Lukic. You earlier said five names were clearly wrong. What did you mean by that? Is that these people that you established that they were not detained or they were not -- their fate was not, as the witness said. Or is it that they were placed in wrong groups or -- by the witness. Which of the two did you refer to?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think the last one. That they are mixed up in [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They are mixed up in the groups. I think I earlier said that the Chamber was not assisted by further exploring that. Whether it's three or five is not a -- is not matter that counts very much. We will...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, we'll take a break, and the Chamber expects you to finish your cross-examination in today's session. We turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Lukic, if there's anything in the informal communication this morning --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I checked. This is right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's right. Then the only remaining question is whether any of the two should be under seal or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'll check that immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so. Provisionally the two are under seal. Status will be changed once we've heard that there is no need for that. Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I tried to verify data Judge Fluegge was asking me before the break. And we -- we were not able to enter the Tribunal site so I couldn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can tell that you access to the Tribunal site today causes a serious problem for everyone --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- so, therefore, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: To avoid a misunderstanding, I was referring to the Krnojelac transcript, not today's transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's -- Krnojelac's transcript, that's what we tried to [Overlapping speakers] but we couldn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Many of us are using the Internet site of the Tribunal which is by far easier for access to transcripts which are public, so I fully understand what you are saying, Mr. Lukic. You'll have an opportunity to further deal with the matter. Please proceed at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Can we now have 1D792 in e-court, page 37. Which is page 2969 of the transcript from the Krnojelac case of the 13th of February, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In line 25, when you speak of the groups, you say, and I will read it in English: "A. [In English] I saw people being taken out and I knew what had happened to those ..." Then we have to move to another page now. Actually, the second one. Since that one before was blank. And I quote again: "... first group, and I absolutely lacked the courage to listen to that again. "Q. So after the first group, you did not hear anything, is it merely your assumption that the same thing happened as with the first group? "A. Absolutely." [Interpretation] Do you accept that part of your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you described the first group. What I find unclear is that you said that they were being beaten up in there, that you saw them being carried out in blankets, and then that you heard shots after they were taken out. All of this can be found in your 1995 statement, page 8, paragraph 2 of the English version; page 8, paragraph 3 of the B/C/S version. This is P982. This is my question: In your view, were -- did these people who were in the first group succumb to the beatings, or were they killed outside of the main building?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: I think that they succumbed to the beatings, and after they left the rooms where they were beaten, they were probably also shot. If there were nine person, you'd always hear nine shots.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're asking about the view of the witness and what he now he says that what he thinks. Let's stick to the facts. Let's stick to the facts and let's ask him what he observed, what he knows.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your view, it was the guards who participated in the killings, and it was always the same guards; right?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Well, the ones that I could recognise were guards. Whether somebody else participated in this as well is something I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You say that some of the bodies were also exhumed.

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the second, third, and fourth groups now. Is it not correct that you do not know because you did not observe who was killed in what manner?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: My assumption is that they were killed by being beaten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's resist to assume all kind of things. And if you would refrain, as you did again, Mr. Lukic, asking "in your view." You're eliciting opinion. What the witness can tell us, let him tell it. What he thinks and concludes is, at this moment, not relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for you to know, it is not that the Chamber says what you think is wrong or right, but the Chamber will establish what happened on the basis of factual knowledge of the witnesses, and then, later on, you'll find out whether your thoughts are the same as the conclusions the Chamber will draw.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We established your knowledge about these killings. I'd like to go back to you personally now. Let's briefly discuss the times that you were beaten in the KP Dom. In your first statement that from 1995 you say that you were beaten up twice. In the second statement you said that you were beaten three times. In the trial against Krnojelac, you said that you were beaten four times.

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Yes. And that is correct: Four times.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So, in this case, what you stated in the Krnojelac case is not -- is correct rather than what you stated in your statement.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness repeat his answer, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Before we invite the witness to repeat his answer, Ms. MacGregor.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: I don't want to belabour the issue, but he's just said what you stated in the Krnojelac case is correct. There is a significant chunk of testimony about the beatings in general in that testimony, and anticipating the line of this questioning, I think it's important that it's very clear what the witness is actually confirming that he said before versus what he said today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now could you please -- well, perhaps you rephrase the question. What apparently is the case - and I am addressing both parties now - that there are inconsistencies in the details about names and events, et cetera, et cetera. If the parties agree on that, we can just simply ask the witness what explains that instead of spending half an hour or more on establishing such inconsistencies or contradictions or incompleteness. I mean, if the parties would agree on the differences then we could keep things far shorter. Now you're saying we need all the details. If you would sit together with Mr. Lukic and say, Well, looking at it, it is obvious that this is it what the witness did, that is what the witness did, then you can put it as such to him, ask for further comments on it, and then move on, instead of spending days and days -- no, no, I'm exaggerating, Mr. Lukic. Considerable time on these matters to be established. Could the parties keep this in mind and could you rephrase your lasts question, Mr. Lukic, and put it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness said that the information that he was the beaten up four times is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me put this to you. The third time that you were beaten, according to you, was -- actually, when was that you were beaten up for the third time?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: In November.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Because I had sewn socks out of sheets.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the counsel switch on the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at your 1996 statement. That's P983. In both these versions, it is on page 3. Now it is marked as paragraph 7. And you say: "So many things happened in -- at KP Dom during my detention that it didn't seem important to mention this. All the time the prisoners were punished and locked into solitary confinement, even for every minor point. For instance, when the prisoners Safet Avdic, Rasim Hanjalic, and Ibrahim Kafedzic made socks out of blankets they were punished." On this occasion, were you, too, punished.

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Well, I don't see what the problem is here. They were punished first and then I was punished later.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You talk about this in your statement.

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Well, yes, I described them but I did not mention my own case in this -- for the first time in this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So what is in the statement is not correct. Rather, what is correct is what you said in court.

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Well, the statement is correct. Rasim Safet Avdic and Ibrahim Kafedzic, they were the first to be taken out because of this act.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you talk about other people but you don't mention yourself while discussing -- while talking about the same event.

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Well, you do have this correction that was added to my statement. I did explain this, and I said that then I did the same thing and then I was punished, and that was on the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Milun Miljanovic -- it says Miljun in the statement?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Well, it is Milun.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Milun Miljanovic, he was the deputy to Dragan Gagovic, the chief of police in Foca; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You saw him issuing orders to soldiers.

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know who those soldiers were?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: I knew one or two of them. They were sappers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know what authorised the deputy SUP commander to command the army?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Milun Miljanovic was in that same function before the war. He was the deputy police commander. Now what his role was -- this was before the war, now what his role was during the war, what his post was, I don't know. I heard that he was Gagovic's deputy, but how it was that he found himself in this group of sappers at the KP Dom, I really don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would now like briefly to refer you to the part where you cleaned the rooms that people had left from. Do you recall when this happened? When was it that they cleaned these rooms?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: I don't know what rooms you mean because I had to sweep or clean many rooms.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, it's about that case where people in June left those rooms. We can take a look at your statement. That's the 1995 statement. P982.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need page 10 in the B/C/S version, the first paragraph, and the tenth page in English, the first paragraph as well. Obviously we need paragraph 47. In my version that's on page 10 in B/C/S, but here I see that we need page 9. That's probably the last paragraph on that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Here, you state, and you see that they talk about taking away the four groups. And you say: "About a week after the incidents, a guard called me out and ordered me to clean the room where the people had been beaten to death. I saw the floor was -- in that room was covered with blood."

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see 1D792, please. That's in e-court. Again, that will be the Krnojelac transcript of 13 February 2001. We need page 41 in e-court. And the transcript page is 2973.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In line 5 toward the end of that sentence, you say: [In English] "I told I already said that I cleaned those rooms in August. I don't remember the date. "Q. So it was two months after all this had happened? "A. Yes, correct."

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It is the month of August. I didn't hear you saying that it was these seven days later. But it is correct that it was in August.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Here, you were asked -- so it was two months after all this had happened? That's when you cleaned that?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is this -- so was it two months after the incident or seven days after the incident?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Well, it was two months after the incident. So this all happened in late June and early July. So it's not really a full two months. Maybe a month and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So what is in your statement that only seven days this elapsed between the incidents and your cleaning, that's incorrect?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: No, no, that's not correct. The statement is specific about when this happened and I stand by it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's see what the statement says. [In English]now I do have the reference for -- Judge Fluegge asked for me. It's in 1D793, e-court page 95, line 13, where this witness as members of the second group mentioned Seval Soro, Mate Ivancic, Zulfo Veiz, Ekrem Tulek, and Refik Cankusic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: With the addition that he said: "I'm not sure I can remember all of them."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, because he gave only five names -- five names out of nine. [Interpretation] Please bear with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I believe Judge Fluegge said I can't be -- remember all of them. Not "I can" remember all of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's hereby corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I thought you would put that to the witness and then put your question. Which you did in relation to the question you cited earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I just got data on my question list, so I don't have the transcript in front of me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. But you were invited, when Judge Fluegge raised the issue, to put that to the witness and not to refer him to an earlier portion of his testimony which he was not aware of -- at least the text was not, so to put it in detail on all the matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, but, yeah the system didn't work. Obviously it started to work --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The system --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- but I didn't got that [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, here you said -- which page was it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's page -- it's our 1D793.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's page 94 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Line -- line 13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And this is on the screen now. We had it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We had it on the screen and this is -- this would be now the appropriate basis for putting the question to the witness that he, indeed, mentioned these names. Now it's -- it has appeared now. It's back at line 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. And now should I read it, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, you did it already.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And we all can see the names, but now it's a quotation of his answer --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- in that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And now you should put a -- use this information --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- put it to the witness and [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that would be my last question. Thank you for your help.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, on page 2862 of the Krnojelac transcript, in your testimony, you said in line 13 -- in line 12 there is a question that was put to you. Or rather, let's begin with line 10. "Q. [In English] How many were called out on this occasion? "A. Nine again. "Q. And do you recall who was called out? "A. Seval Soro, Mate Ivancic, Zulfo Veiz, Ekrem Tulek, Mandzo -- no, not Mandzo. Cankusic, Refik. I'm not sure I can remember all of them." [Interpretation] so were these men in the second group or some other men? Can you recall at all, as you sit here.

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: No, these were not the ones. Ivancic -- Mate Ivancic was in the third group.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. You are now cross-checking this by comparing it with the list that you have before you, the statement. Do you remember these names as you sit here today?

utterances.speaker: RM013
utterances.text: Well, I do remember that they were taken out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Microphone -- well, that's -- well, then we would not have on the -- on the transcript that this concludes your --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is the conclusion of our cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was missing on the -- missing on the transcript now. Could I ask you, Ms. MacGregor, in view of the Chamber's observations and in view of now the last portion of the cross-examination, could you inform us how much time you would need tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I anticipate it could be as short as ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the witness also is aware of approximately what he can expect for tomorrow. Thank you. Witness RM013, we'll adjourn for the day, and we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning, and it will not be very long. It will only be less than half an hour all together. I would like to instruct you that you should not speak or communicate in any other way with whoever about your testimony, whether that is testimony you've given today or testimony still to be given tomorrow. Mr. Groome, anything to be raised before we go into closed session?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just a few seconds, Your Honour. With respect to P990 and P991, which the Chamber admitted earlier in the session, they do not need to be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So P990 and P991 are public exhibits. We turn into closed session and adjourn from there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 20th day of February, 2013, at 9.30 a.m.
